programOutcomes: PO1: Demonstrate fundamental knowledge of plant diversity, structure, function and classification.
PO2: Apply botanical concepts to explain biological processes at cellular, organismal and ecosystem levels.
PO3: Develop scientific thinking, analytical ability and problem-solving skills in biological sciences.
PO4: Conduct basic laboratory techniques, experiments and field studies using standard botanical tools.
PO5: Interpret, analyze and present biological data using appropriate methods and scientific terminology.
PO6: Understand the role of plants and microorganisms in environment, agriculture, industry and human welfare.
PO7: Apply ethical principles, environmental awareness and sustainability concepts in biological practices.
PO8: Communicate scientific knowledge effectively through oral, written and visual formats.
PO9: Develop teamwork, leadership and lifelong learning skills relevant to biological sciences.
PO10: Prepare for higher education, research and careers in botany, biotechnology, agriculture and allied fields.

taxonomySet.name: Remember
taxonomySet.description: Recall facts, basic concepts and definitions.

taxonomySet.name: Understand
taxonomySet.description: Explain ideas or concepts in one’s own words.

taxonomySet.name: Apply
taxonomySet.description: Use information in new or practical situations.

taxonomySet.name: Analyze
taxonomySet.description: Break information into parts and examine relationships.

taxonomySet.name: Evaluate
taxonomySet.description: Justify decisions or evaluate based on criteria.

chapters.title: Diversity of Microbes
chapters.description: Study of viruses, bacteria, cyanobacteria and their structure, reproduction and economic importance.
learningObjectives: Understand the basic structure of viruses and bacteria.
Differentiate between viruses and cellular organisms.
Explain modes of reproduction in bacteria.
Recognise the role of microbes in industry and environment.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Understand the structural organization of viruses and microorganisms.
CO2: Explain modes of reproduction in bacteria and cyanobacteria.
CO3: Differentiate between viruses and cellular microorganisms.
CO4: Evaluate the economic and ecological importance of microbes.

chapters.title: Algae
chapters.description: Classification, structure, reproduction and economic importance of algae.
learningObjectives: Classify algae based on pigments and reserve food.
Describe structure and reproduction in major algal groups.
Explain ecological and commercial importance of algae.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Classify algae based on pigments, reserve food and habitat.
CO2: Describe structural organization of major algal groups.
CO3: Explain reproductive strategies in algae.
CO4: Assess the ecological and commercial importance of algae.

chapters.title: Fungi
chapters.description: General features, classification, reproduction and importance of fungi.
learningObjectives: Understand the general structure of fungi.
Explain various modes of reproduction in fungi.
Describe beneficial and harmful roles of fungi.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Identify general characteristics and classification of fungi.
CO2: Explain structure and reproduction in different fungal groups.
CO3: Differentiate beneficial and harmful fungi.
CO4: Apply knowledge of fungi in agriculture, medicine and industry.

chapters.title: Bryophytes
chapters.description: Study of bryophytes with respect to structure, reproduction and life cycle.
topics: Structure of Riccia, Marchantia and Funaria
learningObjectives: Explain the position of bryophytes in plant kingdom.
Describe life cycle and reproduction in bryophytes.
Understand the concept of alternation of generations.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Explain the position of bryophytes in plant evolution.
CO2: Describe morphology and anatomy of representative bryophytes.
CO3: Explain life cycle and alternation of generations in bryophytes.
CO4: Recognize ecological importance of bryophytes.

chapters.title: Pteridophytes
chapters.description: Morphology, anatomy and reproduction of pteridophytes.
topics: Structure of Lycopodium, Selaginella and Fern
learningObjectives: Understand the evolution of vascular tissues.
Explain reproduction and life cycle of pteridophytes.
Describe the significance of heterospory.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Describe structural features of pteridophytes.
CO2: Explain reproduction and life cycle in pteridophytes.
CO3: Understand the concept of heterospory and seed habit.
CO4: Evaluate evolutionary significance of pteridophytes.

chapters.title: Gymnosperms
chapters.description: Study of gymnosperms with reference to structure, reproduction and economic importance.
learningObjectives: Differentiate gymnosperms from angiosperms.
Describe reproductive structures of gymnosperms.
Explain ecological and economic importance.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Explain general characteristics and classification of gymnosperms.
CO2: Describe morphology and anatomy of Cycas and Pinus.
CO3: Explain reproductive processes in gymnosperms.
CO4: Assess ecological and economic importance of gymnosperms.

chapters.title: Angiosperms – Introduction and Classification
chapters.description: Introduction to flowering plants and their classification.
learningObjectives: Understand basic features of angiosperms.
Explain the basis of classification systems.
Differentiate monocot and dicot plants.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Explain basic characteristics of angiosperms.
CO2: Understand principles of angiosperm classification.
CO3: Differentiate monocotyledons and dicotyledons.
CO4: Interpret floral characters for plant identification.

chapters.title: Plant Cell Biology
chapters.description: Study of plant cell structure and cell organelles.
topics: Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus and ribosomes
learningObjectives: Describe structure and function of plant cell organelles.
Understand differences between plant and animal cells.
Explain role of cell organelles in metabolism.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Describe ultra-structure of plant cells.
CO2: Explain functions of cell organelles.
CO3: Differentiate plant and animal cells.
CO4: Relate cellular organization with metabolic functions.
